explanations.1: This checks if the mod_deflate module is available on the server before trying to use it.
explanations.3: This is a nested check to see if mod_filter is available, which allows more precise control over which file types get compressed.
explanations.4: This tells the server to compress these specific file types (fonts, scripts, images, etc.) to make them smaller when sent to users' browsers.
explanations.10: This turns on the gzip compression feature for servers using mod_gzip instead of mod_deflate.
explanations.11: This allows the server to handle compressed data that might be split into chunks, ensuring everything decompresses correctly.
explanations.12: This tells mod_gzip to compress files matching these extensions like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.
explanations.13: This compresses output from CGI scripts, which are programs that generate dynamic content on the server.
explanations.14: This compresses anything labeled as 'text' type (like plain text, HTML, CSS, JavaScript) by matching the beginning of the MIME type.
explanations.20: This prevents image files from being compressed since they're usually already compressed and compressing them again wastes resources.
explanations.21: This re-includes SVG images (which are text-based, not binary) for compression, overriding the previous exclusion for images.
explanations.22: This prevents double-compression by skipping files that are already marked with gzip encoding to avoid corrupting them.
